newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Switzerland says seized cargo includes gene-soy.
newsitem.headline: Switzerland says seized cargo includes gene-soy.

text.p: Swiss police on Wednesday said tests of soymeal seized from a Rhein river barge last week showed it contained traces of genetically modified soy that has not been approved for marketing in Switzerland.
Basle canton (state) police said the 250 tonnes of soymeal would remain impounded as authorities investigate whether the import broke any laws.
"The cantonal laboratory found genetically modified material made up about one percent of each sample," a police spokesman said.

Genetically altered soybeans are not yet allowed as food or fodder in Switzerland, although the Federal Health Office is expected to rule soon on an application to market the modified soy by its developer, U.S. chemical group Monsanto.
But genetically modified organisms may be imported for processing as long as they are re-exported later.

Swiss authorities impounded the barge last Thursday after Greenpeace activists tried for hours to prevent it from entering Switzerland, claiming it was illegally importing genetically modified soybeans.
Basle prosecutors ordered the cargo sealed in a grain silo pending an investigation of Greenpeace's charges and released the boat.
The new type of bean was developed by Monsanto to be resistant to its own new "super weedkiller" Roundup.

Environmental groups describe the Roundup technology as a risky experiment with nature while the Monsanto strain has been given a clean bill of health by the U.S. and European Union authorities, who say it poses no danger to the human food chain.
